expectations.text: Outputs exactly one JSON code block for the progress
expectations.evidence: Exactly one fenced code block (```json); no other code blocks in the reply.

expectations.text: The JSON validates: `python3 scripts/progress_tool.py validate <file>` reports no errors (grader runs it)
expectations.evidence: Saved to /tmp/closebook-eval22.json. `progress_tool.py validate` reported "progress file: VALID (0 errors, 0 warnings)" (exit 0). `due --date 2026-11-01` (the tool uses --date, not --today) listed kp3 weak priority_flag yes, kp2 fuzzy, kp1 solid, all next_review 2026-11-01, 0 days overdue.

expectations.text: Uses only core fields (no extension-only fields such as method or interaction on attempts), unless the user asked for the full version
expectations.evidence: Compared against progress.schema.json. Every field used is tier core: top level (schema_version, profile, topic, language, created, updated, settings, knowledge_points, weak_points); knowledge_point (id, title, importance, knowledge_type, status, mastery, leitner_box, next_review, last_reviewed, priority_flag, attempts, errors); attempt (id, at, phase, result, hint_level, confidence, error_type). No extension fields (no method, interaction, question, note, sessions, efficiency). The error_entry sub-fields sit under the core `errors` property.

expectations.text: kp1 is in box 1 with next_review 2026-11-01; kp2 and kp3 are weak or fuzzy in box 1 with next_review 2026-11-01; kp3 has a high-confidence error noted (priority / weak_points note)
expectations.evidence: kp1: leitner_box 1, next_review 2026-11-01. kp2: mastery fuzzy, box 1, 2026-11-01. kp3: mastery weak, box 1, 2026-11-01, priority_flag true, errors[0].high_confidence true, and the weak_points note "...信心 3 答错". `high-confidence-errors` lists kp3 misconception, still_flagged yes.

expectations.text: The diagnostic attempt has phase diagnostic and does not change the schedule
expectations.evidence: kp3-1 has phase "diagnostic", result "dont_know" and no confidence. `recompute --dry-run` reproduced the same mastery/box/next_review/priority_flag for all points, so the diagnostic attempt has no effect on the schedule. The only difference is weak_points order (saved kp3,kp2; recomputed kp2,kp3).

expectations.text: Tells the user to save it and paste it back in a new chat, and gives the next review date(s) as absolute dates
expectations.evidence: "保存好这段（复制到备忘录之类的地方就行），下次新开对话时粘贴回来" and "2026-11-01（明天）：先 kp3...再 kp2...最后 kp1": an absolute date.

expectations.text: Does not claim it will remember the progress itself
expectations.evidence: "我在新的对话里不会记得今天的内容，下面这段就是你的存档。" It explicitly disclaims memory.

notes: Excellent. The JSON is compact single-line core-profile data, validates cleanly, and replays to the identical schedule. The reply correctly avoids crediting synthesis free recall to any single point and explains why all three are due tomorrow. Review order in the text (kp3 → kp2 → kp1) matches the tool's priority order. Remedies match error types (misconception → contrast example; memory lapse → re-retrieve). Factual content is correct: in TCP Reno, three duplicate ACKs trigger fast retransmit/recovery (ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd ≈ ssthresh), not cwnd = 1, which only happens on a timeout. Congestion avoidance adds about 1 MSS per RTT. Minor: no file-download promise, appropriate for the no-file environment. The weak_points order differs from the tool's canonical order, which is harmless.
